trust_decision.summary: Whether a request may share or observe cached prefix blocks is decided per engine request by its cache_salt (mixed into the first block hash in vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:605-607 and taken from the EngineInput in vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py:428), so the frontend must attach the caller's salt to every EngineInput it derives; the harmony built-in-tool follow-up at vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py:713-717 rebuilds the input with tokens_input(token_ids) and drops it, so every turn after the first tool call falls back to the unsalted cross-tenant cache.

landing_point.why: The report names harmony tool continuations dropping cache_salt; this loop is the only place a Responses turn is re-rendered after a built-in tool call, and it is where the salt set on the first turn (serving.py:760) is lost.

fix_sites.entry_point: OnlineRenderer.render_responses (shared render API used by both Responses servings)
POST /v1/responses/render on the render-only server (vllm launch render)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The renderer-side helper and the /v1/responses/render transport are a render-only lane in vllm/renderers with no /v1/responses route at this commit, so a solver can argue the report only names the stateful tool loop and leave the second implementation (and the render-only server) untouched.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Requests that omit cache_salt must keep sharing the default prefix cache (documented as the 'No salt' behaviour), and the chat-completions harmony renderer at vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py:220-267 must keep its existing per-request salting; an over-broad fix that salts every continuation or substitutes a default/per-request salt breaks that reuse.

O6_input_shapes: input as a plain string vs a list of input items
harmony history (openai_harmony Message list) vs chat history (dict list), rejected when mismatched
first turn (preamble built) vs continuation (stored history reused)
one built-in tool round vs repeated tool rounds in the same request (salt must survive turn 2 onward)
salted request (cache_salt set) vs unsalted request (cache_salt None)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new ConversationContext whose follow-up turn re-renders its own engine input (like HarmonyContext.render_for_completion here, or ParsableContext at context.py:557) without the salt
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: each context type owns its re-render, so a maintainer adding a context for a new parser/tool mode writes its own tokens_input call and can forget the salt

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another decode-side fast path (the reuse_ids early return) that rebuilds tokens_input directly instead of going through render_chat_async
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: this early-return path already bypasses the templating path that forwards prompt_extras, so a second fast path added later is the obvious place to drop cache_salt

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a fourth generate-side branch that builds mm_input/embeds_input from a GenerateRequest without copying cache_salt
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: there are already three branches here and two of them set the salt by hand rather than through prompt_extras

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the Rust server lowering a render request into a GenerateRequest (it copies cache_salt today at render.rs:103) gains a Responses or tool-loop route
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: rust/src/server already duplicates chat/completions, completions and render routes in another language, so the same check has to be re-written there
